newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Lee scorns China's "wishful thinking".
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Lee scorns China's "wishful thinking".

text.p: President Lee Teng-hui assailed Beijing on Thursday for trying to force Taiwan to accept communist China's sovereignty, saying national unification can spring only from democracy, freedom and equitable prosperity.
"Nothing good will come out of one side forcing its will on the other," Lee told a reception marking Hong Kong's handover to Beijing sovereignty.

Saying consensus could be found in rival proposals made by himself and Chinese President Jiang Zemin in 1995, Lee scorned Beijing's willingness to retake Taiwan by force as a "hegemonic attitude" that threatened bilateral ties and Asia's security.
"Taiwan, the Chinese mainland, Hong Kong and Macau must be united under the principles of democracy freedom and equitable prosperity," Lee said.
"Until this ultimate goal is realised, neither of the two political entities on the two sides of the Taiwan strait is subordinate to the other."
Lee, the first popularly elected leader in Chinese history, heads the exiled Republic of China that fled the mainland for Taiwan in 1949 after Nationalists lost a civil war to the communists.

Lee said Taiwan would not be absorbed Hong Kong-style by the mainland, rejecting the "one country, two systems" model local autonomy that Beijing is implementing in Hong Kong and Macau and holds out as a model for Taiwan's "return to the motherland".
"While Beijing may have applied its One Country, Two Systems formula to establish its rule in Hong Kong, its plan to take the same approach with Taiwan is mere wishful thinking," he said.
Under Taiwan's democracy, Taipei had to accept the will of the people, the "vast majority" of whom did not support Beijing's scheme for reunification, Lee said.
Vice President Lien Chan has offered a new twist on Beijing's formula, saying union was possible under "one country, one good system" -- multiparty democracy -- across China.
Lien, speaking at the same reception, urged Beijing to end a 24-month freeze on bilateral contacts and allow Hong Kong to act as a cross-straits intermediary.
"It is a matter of either creating a win-win situation or playing a losing game for all three sides," Lien said.

Lee's address capped the first day of an international media blitz aiming to tap into a worldwide focus on Hong Kong's July 1 handover and its implications for Taiwan. Nearly 300 foreign journalists have come to Taiwan for a weeklong media tour.
Lee urged relaxation of China's iron-fisted communist rule.

"We believe that all Chinese people will welcome reform and liberalisation on the mainland just as they will welcome the consolidation of democracy and economic liberalisation on Taiwan and continued progress and prosperity in Hong Hong," Lee said.
Lee said Taiwan's freedom and democracy, which have replaced martial law and authoritarian Nationalist Party rule since 1987, could not be ignored or negated.
"We shall never give up our democratic institutions, just as we will never abandon our hope for peace," he said.
Lee repeated his willingness to make a "journey of peace" to the mainland but said Beijing had yet to respond favourably.
